newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWF third Australia barley forecast up at 6.45 MT.
newsitem.headline: AWF third Australia barley forecast up at 6.45 MT.

text.p: Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd (AWF) has increased its forecast of Australia's 1997/98 barley production to 6.445 million tonnes from its previous forecast of 6.270 million tonnes.
This compares with revised Australian production of 6.632 million tonnes in 1996/97.
Conditions for seeding Australian barley had been very good over the past month, despite meteorological predictions of a dry Australian spring, AWF said.
Australian farmers in most states have had sufficient rainfall now, not only to seed their barley crops, but also to anticipate payable yields, it said.
If there were to be a spring (September/October) drought, it was more likely to affect the 1998/99 barley crop than the crop now in the ground, it said.
If Australia did have a drought, it would be unusual for it to occur on the east coast and the west coast in the same year, it said.
Queensland barley crops had been sown with the advantage of subsoil moisture in sufficient amounts to almost guarantee average yields at least, AWF said.
Some farms were still waiting for rain to moisten the surface soil and allow for cultivating.
All areas of New South Wales (NSW) had now had enough rain to be able to proceed to the completion of barley sowing, it said.
The last area to complete seeding would be the south-west of the state.
Victorian barley areas had been sown under ideal conditions, with some crops having already emerged evenly and with a harvest already assured, it said.
In South Australia, rainfall had been patchy and well below average, and not yet enough for all growers to be able to conclude seeding, it said.
However, on paddocks that have received early rain the crops are already through, one clear month earlier than was possible last season.
Growers who have not been able to complete seeding have been applying fertiliser, indicating strong intentions to seed planned barley paddocks, AWF said.
The start of the barley cropping season in Western Australia had been excellent, it said.
The only area where barley seeding was not complete was the Geraldton area, not an important barley area, it said.
The long growing season in Western Australia should help malting barley quality.
AWF's 1996/97 estimates have been adjusted to the recently-released Australian Bureau of Statistics survey of growers for that season.
